description: Hello! We are 2 high school students who wants to be one of the inventors in the world. As our motto being "Helping humanity is the best thing you can do", we would like to make humanity and human life easier, safer and much more habitable. Being helpful for the humanity is the best thing we could ever achieve and we will do everything we can in order to reach our goal.
summary: Our project consists of a data shuffler (a python script to create randomized, consisted human values) a backend (a python script which processes the values and checks for any health problems) and a frontend (html + js + css). The frontend is specifically designed for touch-screens and easily controllable via a touchscreen.
details:
1.1 Main Introduction to Software

We choose name "PULSE" because the we think all refreshing values are also a pulse in other terms.

We created our project by considering these main ideas:

  • The system must support multiple astronauts.
  • Each astronaut must maintain an independent physiological state.
  • Astronaut profiles and simulation scenarios must be managed independently.
  • ISS cabin environmental data and space-related data must be shared.
  • Physiological measurements must evolve over time.
  • Multiple abnormalities must be able to occur simultaneously.
  • Health conditions must be detected from actual measurement values rather than scenario names.
  • Missing, invalid, and outdated measurements must be identified separately.
  • Synthetic ECG data must be generated.
  • Results must be exposed through a REST API for frontend applications.
  • Multiple astronauts must be evaluated independently.
  • External real-world data sources must remain distinguishable from synthetic measurements.
  • The system must not make medical diagnoses; it should only report observed conditions and relevant information.

We divided the system as 4 main parts:

  1. shuffler.py (v2.1.0): This python script defines the variables, all types of values that sensors will give to us in real life, and a series of diseases which may happen in space missions. Runs as a client, you can create abnormalities using commands such as "user1 abnormal hyperglycemia"
  2. condition_engine.py: This python script runs as a decision system. It gathers the data from the shuffler.py and evaluates it to decide is the astronaut having some medical issues or not. The end user can't directly communicate with this file.
  3. main.py (v0.4.0): This python script acts as a provider for frontend. The data processed in condition_engine.py is stamped and sent to frontend via API.
  4. Frontend: Supports touch-screens and specifically designed for touchscreen environments. Users can log into their account and see both their health status and other crew members health status. Astronauts can add a family photo to main dashboard so they can remember their family too.

One of the most important things about this project is it can work fully locally. No connection is required for health proccessing to work. But having a connection helps the medical engineers in Earth to see the status of the astronauts, create graphs, and process the results more professionally at NASA Space Center.

1.2 A More Detailed Look Into Software

shuffler.py is responsible for creating random sensor data, since we don't have access to any sensor right know. This part take most of our time since giving randomized numbers won't be real and may cause unrealities in tests. So we worked on shuffler.py by considering these specifications:

  1. Values must change how it can in real life. So a blood glucose change from 60mg/dL to 110mg/dL in 20ms is not real and may cause problems while testing the software.
  2. Values must change physiologically. An increase in heart rate (BPM) should also increase respiratory flow
  3. All values should be in healthy condition (unless we specifically chose abnormality)
  4. More than one abnormality may happen at the same time, if they are not opposite to each other. In example, hypertension and hypotension can't happen at the same time but hypertension and hyperglycemia can.
  5. Values can be gathered in different times. For an example, ECG requires data refreshing for 500hz (around 2ms) but SpO2 can be refreshed every 5 to 10 minutes.

condition_engine.py is responsible for evaluating the raw values coming from shuffler.py and decide is there an abnormality happening or not. It does not check for only one variable, since an abnormality may seem by checking more than one variable at a time.

main.py is responsible for API for frontend communication. Frontend requests the data from the API, main.py requests the evaluation results and raw data from condition_engine.py, timestamps them, asks for NASA's DONKI API, RedLab API for space weather and radiation; and Open-Notify API for locating ISS. Then main.py gives these results as JSON to frontend.

Frontend is specifically astronaut oriented, with much easier and understandable UI design. UX is more user-friendly and easy to control. It is specifically designed for touch-surfaces, so astronauts can control the UI by their hands. Warnings and all types of cautions can seen as bubble notifications. Astronauts can see other crew members health status. If there is a life-threathening situation, other crew members are notified about this via their watches, they can go to the astronaut and make medical intervention. UI also shows what to do to crew members.

1.3 What Can Be Added or Improved

Our system currently have some bugs because of limited-time, but most of the functionality is working without a problem. In the future, gathering these values from sensors will be a great improvement. We're looking to improve our application after the hackatlon and make it more usable and more real

1.4 Who Are We?

We're 2 high schoolers from Türkiye who wants to improve human life and welfare. We're looking forward to join other competitions and all types of contest improving human welfare. We're very appreciated to be part of this community and would like to join next year. See you there!
